x: A Presidential reference under Article 143 yields only an advisory opinion, not a binding judgment.

s: The Muslim Women Act, 1986 was enacted by Parliament after which Supreme Court judgment?
x: Parliament passed the Muslim Women Act 1986 after Shah Bano; the SC/ST (PoA) Amendment 2018 followed Subhash Kashinath Mahajan.

s: Under which Article does the Supreme Court give an advisory opinion on a Presidential reference?
x: An Article 143 reference yields only an advisory opinion, which is not binding.

s: Which case laid down the basic structure limit on Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368?
x: Kesavananda Bharati held that an amendment under Article 368 cannot alter the basic structure.

s: In which year did Public Interest Litigation begin in India, with a case filed on behalf of prisoners?
x: PIL began in 1979 with a case filed on behalf of prisoners; its basis lies in Articles 32, 226 and 142.

s: Who gave the typology of ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation and democratic fears about judicial activism?
x: Upendra Baxi gave this typology of fears; it does not include an 'electoral' fear.

s: Which of the following pairs of case and guideline subject is correctly matched?
x: Prakash Singh dealt with police reforms. Vishaka concerned workplace sexual harassment and T.S.R. Subramanian civil-services safeguards.

s: The Vishaka guidelines continued to operate in a legislative vacuum until the enactment of which law?
o: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
x: The Vishaka guidelines on workplace sexual harassment operated until the POSH Act was enacted in 2013.

s: Public Interest Litigation may attract criticism when it is used mainly for which purpose?
o: Protection of fundamental rights through judicial review
Constitutional interpretation in genuine public causes
x: PIL is criticised when it is misused for publicity or political purposes rather than for a genuine public cause or protection of rights.

s: Civil Services Boards and fixed tenure for civil servants were directed in which case?
x: T.S.R. Subramanian (2013) directed Civil Services Boards and fixed tenure.

s: Public Interest Litigation in India rests on which constitutional provisions?
x: PIL is based on Articles 32, 226 and 142.

s: To what do the Prakash Singh (2006) guidelines of the Supreme Court relate?
x: Prakash Singh (2006) laid down police reforms, including fixed DGP tenure.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of Upendra Baxi's fears about judicial activism?
x: Baxi listed ideological, epistemic, management, legitimation and democratic fears, not electoral.

s: Media organisations are generally regarded as stakeholders of governance under which category?
x: Media organisations are counted among civil society stakeholders involved in governance.

s: Pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to which set of governance stakeholders?
x: State, Market and Civil Society are the three broad stakeholder sets, and pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to civil society.

s: In which year was the National Innovation Council established as a Government body?
x: The National Innovation Council was set up in 2010; CPR, NCAER, PRS and ORF are independent bodies.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation — Congress-linked body
x: The Syama Prasad Mookerjee Research Foundation is linked with the BJP, not the Congress. The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation is associated with the Congress.

s: The Centre for Policy Research (CPR) and NCAER are examples of which type of think tank?
x: CPR and NCAER are independent think tanks, not government bodies.

s: Which of the following pairs of think tank and its type is correctly matched?
x: The Rajiv Gandhi Foundation is Congress-linked; CPR and NCAER are independent and the National Innovation Council (2010) is a government body.

s: By upgrading which institute was the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) established?
x: The NCGG was established by upgrading the National Institute of Administrative Research associated with LBSNAA.

s: Where is the Centre for Good Governance, set up by undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2001, located?
x: The CGG, set up with DFID (UK) and the World Bank, is in Hyderabad; New Delhi and Mussoorie are the locations of the National Centre for Good Governance.

s: As what does the Centre for Good Governance (CGG) in Andhra Pradesh mainly function?
o: Statutory commission for recruitment to public services
Governance-reform think tank advising the government
x: The CGG is a governance-reform think tank that advises the government on administrative reforms, e-governance, research and training.

s: Where is the head office of the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG)?
x: NCGG's head office is in New Delhi with a branch at Mussoorie; CGG is in Hyderabad.

s: With the collaboration of which agencies was the Centre for Good Governance set up by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in 2001?
o: UNDP and the Asian Development Bank
x: The CGG was set up in Hyderabad in 2001 with support from DFID (UK) and the World Bank.

s: Which institution was set up by the Government of undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2001 at Hyderabad as a governance-reform think tank?
x: The Centre for Good Governance (CGG), Hyderabad, was set up by AP in 2001 as a think tank on governance reform.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Centre for Good Governance (CGG), Andhra Pradesh:
1. It was set up in 2001.
2. It was set up in collaboration with DFID (UK) and the World Bank.
3. Its head office is at Mussoorie.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: CGG was set up in 2001 with DFID and World Bank support and is based in Hyderabad; Mussoorie is the branch of NCGG.

s: In which year did DARPG introduce the National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment (NeSDA)?
x: NeSDA is a DARPG tool introduced in 2019 to assess e-governance service delivery.

s: What is the name of Andhra Pradesh's WhatsApp-based governance platform offering more than 500 services?
x: Mana Mitra WhatsApp Governance offers 500+ services, with a target of 1,000.

s: Where is the branch office of the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG)?
x: NCGG has its head office in New Delhi and a branch at Mussoorie.

s: Which one of the following correctly represents the World Bank's definition of governance?
o: The manner in which power is exercised in managing a country's economic and social resources for development
The distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
The exclusive exercise of authority by the executive branch
The process by which elections are conducted at regular intervals
x: The World Bank defines governance as the manner in which power is exercised in managing a country's economic and social resources for development.

s: Which institution first brought the concept of 'good governance' into development discourse?
x: B is correct: the World Bank first brought 'good governance' into development discourse through its 1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa (APPSC-GS 2018 key). A, UNDP, gave its own definition later (1997). C and D are not credited with introducing the term.

s: Which body's approach to governance stresses efficiency, effectiveness, equity and sustainability?
x: UNESCAP stresses efficiency, effectiveness, equity and sustainability; the World Bank stresses accountability, transparency and the rule of law.

s: Which of the following distinguishes governance from government?
o: Governance is confined to the state, whereas government includes civil society.
Governance refers only to judicial administration.
Governance is broader and involves the market and civil society, not merely the state.
Government and governance are identical in scope and meaning.
x: Governance is broader than government because it involves the state together with the market and civil society.

s: Democracy aids development mainly by encouraging which of the following?
x: Democracy aids development by encouraging citizen participation and accountability.

s: In its 1989 report on which region did the World Bank first use the term 'good governance'?
x: The World Bank's 1989 report on Sub-Saharan Africa first brought 'good governance' into development use.

s:
Consider the following statements about governance:
1. The World Bank first used the term 'good governance' in 1989.
2. UNDP's definition of governance was given in 1997.
3. Governance is narrower than government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; governance is broader than government, as it involves the state, market and civil society.

s: According to UNDP, which are the three most critical characteristics of good governance?
o: Rule of law, security and decentralisation
x: Transparency, accountability and responsiveness are identified as the three most critical characteristics.

s: Which of the following is one of the eight attributes of good governance in the UN/UNDP list?
x: Consensus orientation is one of the eight UN/UNDP attributes; centralisation, red tapism and secrecy are not features of good governance.

s: Which among the following is NOT a feature of good governance as listed by the UN/UNDP?
x: Centralisation is not a feature; responsiveness, equity and consensus orientation are among the eight UN/UNDP attributes.

s: Among the pillars of good governance, what does 'Ethos' stand for?
x: Ethos means service; ethics means honesty and integrity, equity means empathy for weaker sections, and efficiency means speedy ICT-based delivery.

s: Which of the following is regarded as the most foundational tool for implementing good governance?
x: People's participation is identified as the most foundational tool for implementing good governance; other tools include RTI, Sevottam, Citizen Charters and e-governance.

s: In the four pillars of good governance, what does 'Efficiency' stand for?
x: Efficiency means speedy delivery using ICT; ethics means honesty and integrity, ethos service and equity empathy for weaker sections.

s: After how many years is the Good Governance Index of DARPG, launched on Good Governance Day 2019, to be revised?
x: The GGI, which ranks States, UTs and districts, is to be revised every two years.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the ten sectors of the Good Governance Index?
x: Foreign affairs and diplomacy is not one of the ten GGI sectors. The sectors include citizen-centric governance, environment, public health, agriculture and allied sectors, and others.

s: Whose birthday is observed as Good Governance Day in India?
x: Good Governance Day, 25 December, marks the birthday of Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

s: In which year was Good Governance Day first observed in India?
x: Good Governance Day was announced and first observed in 2014.

s: In the Good Governance Index 2021, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in which sector?
x: In GGI 2021, Andhra Pradesh was 1st in agriculture and allied sectors.

s: Which State topped the composite ranking of the Good Governance Index 2021?
x: Gujarat was 1st in GGI 2021, followed by Maharashtra and Goa.

s: In which year was the Good Governance Index launched by DARPG?
x: DARPG launched the Good Governance Index on Good Governance Day (25 December) 2019.

s: How many indicators were used in the Good Governance Index 2021?
x: GGI 2021, released on 25 December 2021, used 58 indicators across 10 sectors.

s: Which department is identified as India's nodal department for the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
x: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, or DARPG, is India's nodal department for the WGI.

s: Since which year have the Worldwide Governance Indicators been available?
x: The WGI cover more than 200 countries since 1996, with dimensions including Government Effectiveness and Rule of Law.

s: The Worldwide Governance Indicators and V-Dem indices are mainly criticised because they:
o: Rely substantially on expert opinion and perceptions
Measure only economic growth and fiscal deficit
x: WGI and V-Dem are contested because, as perception-based indices, they rely substantially on expert opinion.

s: Which of the following is a dimension of the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators?
x: Regulatory Quality is one of the six WGI dimensions; HDI is not a WGI dimension, and citizen-centric governance is a sector of DARPG's Good Governance Index.

s: How many dimensions do the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators have?
x: The WGI has six dimensions; 8 is the number of UN attributes and 10 the number of GGI sectors.

s: According to WGI 2023, on which dimension did India score low compared with global averages?
x: WGI 2023 placed India moderate on government effectiveness and rule of law but low on political stability.

s: How many countries do the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators cover?
x: The WGI, available since 1996, cover more than 200 countries.

s: What was India's position in the 2026 V-Dem assessment?
o: 100th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral democracy
106th among 154 countries and classified as a liberal democracy
106th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral autocracy
16th among 179 countries and classified as an electoral autocracy
x: The 2026 V-Dem assessment placed India 106th out of 179 and described it as an “electoral autocracy.”

s: What was India's rank in the Responsible Nations Index 2026?
x: India ranked 16th out of 154 countries in the Responsible Nations Index 2026; Singapore ranked first.

s: Who publishes the Good Governance Index?
x: DARPG publishes the Good Governance Index; NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index, DPIIT the BRAP rankings and PAC the Public Affairs Index.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: National MPI — NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI
SDG India Index — University of Gothenburg
x: The National MPI is published by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI. V-Dem is associated with the University of Gothenburg, the Responsible Nations Index with WIF, JNU and IIM Mumbai, and the SDG India Index with NITI Aayog.

s: Who publishes the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) state rankings?
x: BRAP rankings are by DPIIT, not NITI Aayog.

s: Where is the Public Affairs Centre, which publishes the Public Affairs Index, located?
x: The Public Affairs Index is brought out by the Public Affairs Centre (PAC), Bengaluru.

s: Who publishes the V-Dem democracy index?
x: V-Dem is by the University of Gothenburg, not the World Bank.

s: Which pair of index and publisher is correctly matched?
x: The SDG India Index is by NITI Aayog; BRAP is by DPIIT, GGI by DARPG and V-Dem by the University of Gothenburg.

s: Which State topped the first Investment Friendliness Index released by NITI Aayog in 2026?
x: Gujarat ranked first (56.6), followed by Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, in the first Investment Friendliness Index (2026).

s: Who publishes the Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI)?
x: Both the Good Governance Index and GRAI are published by DARPG.

s: Who publishes the Responsible Nations Index?
x: The Responsible Nations Index is brought out by WIF together with JNU and IIM Mumbai.

s: Which country ranked first in the Responsible Nations Index 2026?
x: Singapore was 1st in the Responsible Nations Index 2026; India was 16th of 154.

s: How many indicators does the National Multidimensional Poverty Index of NITI Aayog use?
x: NITI Aayog's National MPI, prepared with UNDP and OPHI, uses 12 indicators.

s: How many pillars does NITI Aayog's first Investment Friendliness Index (2026) have?
x: The Investment Friendliness Index 2026 covered 17 states with 84 indicators grouped in 8 pillars.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Second Administrative Reforms Commission is correctly matched?
x: The Second ARC was set up in 2005 and gave 15 reports; the 4th Report (Ethics in Governance) is of 2007 and the 12th (Citizen Centric Administration) of 2009.

s: What was the title of the Second ARC's 12th Report, which covered Citizen's Charters, grievance redress and the Sevottam model?
o: Promoting e-Governance – The SMART Way Forward
Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
x: The 12th Report (2009), 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance', covered Citizen's Charters, grievance redress, Sevottam and people's participation.

s: Which report of the Second ARC names the barriers to and pre-conditions for good governance?
x: The 12th Report, 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance' (2009), names barriers to and pre-conditions for good governance.

s: Which organisation launched Mission Satyanishta, a programme on ethics in public governance?
x: Mission Satyanishta is an Indian Railways programme on ethics in public governance.

s: Which report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission dealt with codes of ethics and anti-corruption bodies?
x: The 4th Report, 'Ethics in Governance' (2007), dealt with codes of ethics and anti-corruption bodies.
